nodes.summary: There is a finitely generated simple group $G$ that admits a right order, that is, a linear order $\le$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 16.50 positively.
nodes.title: Finitely generated simple right-orderable groups exist

nodes.summary: The statement that there exists a finitely generated simple group $G$ admitting a right order, that is, a linear order $\le$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$. The problem is due to V. M. Kopytov and N. Ya. Medvedev.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.50 (finitely generated simple right-orderable groups)

nodes.summary: The right orders of a group $G$ are the linear orders $\le$ on $G$, viewed as relations, that are invariant under right multiplication: $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$.
nodes.title: Right orders on a group (Kourovka Problem 16.50)

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
